content.text:
Yes, it's a real problem. The box won't come up on its own.

**What the pool log shows:** On boxd, each box runs on its own machine. Here that's `dvm-pool-dfqcve6ztdsmgbd6--sbx-kve3px797apyn0me` at 10.39.14.70. The pool agent keeps trying to reach the box's sandbox agent on port 7302 and the connection is refused every time. I logged into that machine: nothing is listening on 7302, and `discobox-sandbox-agent.service` keeps crashing and restarting (systemd shows it in `auto-restart`). `discobox ls` still shows `sbx_kve3px797apyn0me` as `starting`. The pool agent gives up waiting after 5 minutes, so the box will fail rather than recover.

**Why the agent crashes:** Its journal repeats this every ~2s:

```
systemctl[...]: Failed to try-restart discobox-session-bus.socket: Unit discobox-session-bus.socket not found.
discobox-sandbox-agent: ERROR provision sandbox error="systemctl try-restart discobox-session-bus.socket: exit status 5"
```

At `sandbox-agent/boot/boot.go:156`, the first-boot setup runs `systemctl try-restart discobox-session-bus.socket` and treats any failure as fatal. That unit is only installed by the **desktop** feature (`sandbox-agent/features/desktop/provision.yaml:62`), and this box doesn't have it, so systemctl exits 5 ("unit not found"). The code around it already skips a missing unit:
- `writeSessionBusDropins` in `sandbox-agent/boot/sessionbus.go` checks that the unit exists before writing its drop-in.
- The very next step only starts `discobox-render-proxy-env.service` if its file exists.

The session-bus restart has no such check. That line dates from before the platform was split into optional features, which is probably when it started to break: Docker boxes likely always have the desktop units, so you wouldn't have seen this there.

**Fix:** wrap the restart in the same check:

```go
if fileExists("/etc/systemd/system/discobox-session-bus.socket") {
    if err := b.run("systemctl", "try-restart", "discobox-session-bus.socket"); err != nil {
        return err
    }
}
```

Want me to make that change and add a test for a box without the desktop feature? For this box, either recreate it with the desktop feature or wait for the fix to ship.


content.text:
Here's what's going on and why the fix is needed.

**The cause: on boxd, the desktop installs after the agent's first-boot setup.**

- A Docker box runs from a pre-built image that already contains every feature, including the desktop, so its unit files are always on disk when the sandbox agent first starts.
- A boxd box is a plain machine. The pool copies the platform bundle onto it and runs `discobox-sandbox-agent provision apply`, which installs the features there and then. The desktop feature is marked `async: true` in `sandbox-agent/features/desktop/provision.yaml`, so it installs in the background *after* the agent is ready (the "ready first" change).
- The desktop feature is what installs `discobox-session-bus.socket`: that's the sandbox user's D-Bus session bus, which the desktop and every terminal share.
- The agent's first-boot code (`sandbox-agent/boot/boot.go`) runs `systemctl try-restart discobox-session-bus.socket` and treats any failure as fatal. On a fresh boxd machine that unit doesn't exist yet, so systemctl exits 5, setup fails, and systemd restarts the agent. The next attempt fails the same way. The agent never opens 7302, which is the "connection refused" in your pool log. The line predates the async features, which is why only VM-style boxes hit it.

**What I changed:** the restart now only runs if the unit file is on disk, the same check the next line already does for `discobox-render-proxy-env.service`. That stops the crash loop. `go test ./boot/` passes. I didn't add a test: the boot code uses hard-coded system paths, so there's no easy way to fake a box without the desktop. `check-hooks` reports one failed hook, `review-test-all`, but the failures are in `cli/internal/sandboxcreate` and some git-clone tests that can't reach a local test server ("could not read Username"). Some of those results are stamped 2026-10-23, so at least part of that output is from an earlier run. None of it touches the boot package.

**There's a second problem the guard doesn't fix.** The restart was there so the session bus picks up drop-ins saying it belongs to the sandbox user (`darren`) rather than root. `writeSessionBusDropins` (`sandbox-agent/boot/sessionbus.go`) only writes those drop-ins if the unit already exists. On boxd it doesn't yet, so they're skipped. When the desktop installs later, its session bus will run as root, and a terminal using it as `darren` would probably be refused.

The fix I'd recommend is to write the drop-ins every time, whether or not the unit exists. systemd ignores a drop-in for a unit it doesn't have and applies it once the unit file appears, so the desktop's later install would get the right owner. Then the guarded restart only does real work on images that already have the desktop.

I made the session-bus fix last turn, and it did reach the new box: its sandbox agent is running and listening on 7302. The new box fails at a later step, and it's a separate bug that would also stop any box on a boxd pool.

**Error:** `materialize source "skills": source target: stat /workspace/skill-sources/skills: no such file or directory`

**What's going on:**
- Every new box now gets your project's skills repository as a second Git source, checked out at `/workspace/skill-sources/skills`.
- The sandbox agent's cloner (`sandbox-agent/sourceconverge/converge.go:348`) expects that directory to already exist and fails if it doesn't.
- On Docker, the directory does exist. The pool prepares `/.discobox/sources/<slug>` for each source, and `wireSources` (`sandbox-agent/boot/wire.go:210`) creates the target directory and bind-mounts it there.
- A boxd machine has no `/.discobox/sources` at all; I checked on the machine. So `wireSources` finds nothing to bind, skips the source, and never creates the directory. The clone fails three times and the pool gives up on the create.
- Your main repository doesn't hit this only because it lives at `/workspace` itself, which is created anyway. Any extra source on a VM box would fail the same way.

**Proposed fix:** in `wireSources`, if there is no `/.discobox/sources` at all (a VM box), still create each source's directory, owned by the sandbox user, so the clone has somewhere to go. Keep the current skip for the Docker case, where the pool's directory just hasn't arrived yet.

Two other things:
- The first box, `sbx_kve3px797apyn0me`, is still stuck at `starting` on the old build. I'd remove it.
- From last turn: the session bus would still end up owned by root once the desktop installs. The fix is to write its ownership settings every time.

Want me to make both fixes (the source directory and the session-bus ownership)?

sandbox-agent/DESIGN.md:17:| `boot` | Provisioning a sandbox, from one of two entrypoints, and a third that finishes it on a delivered box's first boot (**`JoinFeatureGroups`**: once the agent has fetched its bundles, the features' wiring and the account's joining of the groups they made, which no tree existed for when `Wire` or `Provision` ran). **`Wire`** is a pool container's boot, the `wire` subcommand `discobox-wire.service` runs from the container's own systemd ([ADR 26-10-10-767](../docs/adr/26-10-10-767-a-container-sandbox-boots-systemd-and-a-unit-wires-its-volumes.md)): it resolves the sandbox user from the bootstrap's `user` and adds it to the manifest's `additionalGroups`, binds the config volume onto `/etc/discobox` (writable: the intake writes there) and the secrets volume onto `/run/discobox/secrets`, wires image-declared data/cache volumes and manifest sources from the primary volumes, creates the working root and gives it to the sandbox user, along with any directory it has to invent on the way to a source target (the image ships the working root root-owned, before that user exists, and a sandbox with no source has no source target under it for anything else to chown), seeds the user's `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.config/direnv/direnv.toml`, and `~/Desktop` launchers, writes the session-bus and desktop drop-ins, and reloads the manager. See ADR 0007. **The sandbox's account is made, never adopted** ([ADR 26-10-16-423](../docs/adr/26-10-16-423-a-harness-is-a-provisioning-bundle-and-the-agent-provisions-any-box.md) §14): an account already exactly the sandbox's (name, uid, gid, home) is kept, and any other holding its uid or name — a provider's image commonly has one at uid 1000, the uid macOS and Windows clients send — is deleted, whenever boot finds one, before the volumes are wired and before the group is resolved (userdel takes the account's own group): logind's sessions for it ended where it has some, what remains at the uid killed, `userdel --force`. Its home goes with it — a plain directory at the sandbox's home path included, so the new account gets `/etc/skel` rather than a dead uid's files — unless it is or contains a mount point or is not a directory the account owns (a system account's); seeding fills the sandbox's home only where it is empty. No account is renamed or given a new uid, gid or home in place, root (uid 0) is never deleted, and a client account named `root` at another uid is refused. A manifest that names no home takes the uid's account's only when that account is the one named (`runuser` completes nothing from an account in the way); otherwise the home is `/home/<name>`. What it deleted is not yet recorded anywhere. **Features first:** before the account, both entrypoints run the box's features' wiring alone (`provision.Boot` with `wireOnly`; see [`provision`](provision/DESIGN.md)) — their groups, so the account joins groups already there, and their env — which also writes `provision.json` saying which features are off; the direnv whitelist, the launchers, and the session-bus and desktop drop-ins are then skipped for a feature it reports off (`booter.off`), and wired as before for one it does not report. A failure there is logged, not fatal: the agent's own run tries again and fails readiness. The unit is ordered before `local-fs.target` and required by `sysinit.target`, so every unit that uses a wired path starts after it; it runs only where the config volume is (`ConditionPathExists=`), and its failure exits the container non-zero (`FailureAction=exit-force`) rather than letting services write into the image layer. It runs on every boot: a container's mounts and account do not survive a restart or a rebuild. Everything it wires comes from the **bootstrap**, `sandbox.json`, which carries the whole create-time config: the config is complete before the wiring runs because the bootstrap carries it, not because the flow fetches it first ([ADR 26-10-08-127](../docs/adr/26-10-08-127-a-sandboxs-bootstrap-is-static-and-the-intake-carries-the-rest.md) §2). Nothing that can change while the sandbox exists is read here — secrets and the proxy credential arrive through the intake once the agent is up. Where there is nothing to wire — a VM guest boots its own init, and its backend places `sandbox.json` through the running guest ([ADR 26-10-09-143](../docs/adr/26-10-09-143-a-vm-sandbox-starts-its-agent-when-its-bootstrap-arrives.md) §1) — **`Provision`** does the same provisioning from the agent's own start: the user and its groups, the working root, the home skeleton, `~/.gitconfig`, direnv config and launchers, and the session-bus and desktop drop-ins — then, systemd having been up since boot, a `daemon-reload`, the session bus's socket recreated for the user, and the proxy-trust environment rendered, which its unit skipped at boot — and nothing wired (no declared volumes, ADR 0126 §2; sources arrive through the intake). It runs once per sandbox: the box's provisioning records (`provision.Records`, `/opt/discobox/provision/sandbox`, on the root filesystem) name the sandbox the disk was provisioned for, so an agent restart (the user's processes running) or a stop and start does not redo it; a disk provisioned before the records were kept carries the `/var/lib/discobox/provisioned` marker they replaced into them once, and the marker is removed. A config volume says `Wire` ran, and then it does nothing; it provisions only a Linux guest, since a macOS or Windows sandbox has one account, the image's (ADR 0145 §5). Also the **export mode**, `discobox-sandbox-agent export <subtree>...` (`export.go`, [ADR 0129](../docs/adr/0129-the-sandbox-agent-reads-the-tree-an-export-carries.md)): PID 1 of a one-shot container the pool agent starts from the sandbox base image, with the agent of the sandbox's platform pin bound in, to read a stopped sandbox's tree. It resolves the declared volumes exactly as `Wire` does — only the sandbox can say where a `%HOME%` path lives — with the user from the `DISCOBOX_USER_*` environment the pool agent gives it, then writes `data` and/or `sources` from the primary volumes to stdout as a `sandboxtree` archive, leaving out each `excludeFromExport` data path's `volumeDir`. It wires, chowns and starts nothing; the trees are mounted read-only, and only the archive goes to stdout, so everything it says goes to stderr, which the pool agent reports when it fails. **`ClearCaches`** is a machine pool's clear-cache, which the server's `POST .../cache/clear` runs: it empties every cache path the bootstrap declares, in place — the declared path, never the volume behind it, so it is the same on a box that wired its volumes and one that did not — keeping each directory, and touches no data path ([ADR 26-10-23-551](../docs/adr/26-10-23-551-a-vm-pool-bootstraps-its-own-agent-from-a-bundle-and-provisions-its-machines.md) §3: a machine's caches are on its own disk). |

See ADR 0007. **The sandbox's account is made, never adopted** ([ADR 26-10-16-423](../docs/adr/26-10-16-423-a-harness-is-a-provisioning-bundle-and-the-agent-provisions-any-box.md) §14): an account already exactly the sandbox's (name, uid, gid, home) is kept, and any other holding its uid or name — a provider's image commonly has one at uid 1000, the uid macOS and Windows clients send — is deleted, whenever boot finds one, before the volumes are wired and before the group is resolved (userdel takes the account's own group): logind's sessions for it ended where it has some, what remains at the uid killed, `userdel --force`. Its home goes with it — a plain directory at the sandbox's home path included, so the new account gets `/etc/skel` rather than a dead uid's files — unless it is or contains a mount point or is not a directory the account owns (a system account's); seeding fills the sandbox's home only where it is empty. No account is renamed or given a new uid, gid or home in place, root (uid 0) is never deleted, and a client account named `root` at another uid is refused. A manifest that names no home takes the uid's account's only when that account is the one named (`runuser` completes nothing from an account in the way); otherwise the home is `/home/<name>`. What it deleted is not yet recorded anywhere. **Features first:** before the account, both entrypoints run the box's features' wiring alone (`provision.Boot` with `wireOnly`; see [`provision`](provision/DESIGN.md)) — their groups, so the account joins groups already there, and their env — which also writes `provision.json` saying which features are off; the direnv whitelist, the launchers, and the session-bus and desktop drop-ins are then skipped for a feature it reports off (`booter.off`), and wired as before for one it does not report. A failure there is logged, not fatal: the agent's own run tries again and fails readiness. The unit is ordered before `local-fs.target` and required by `sysinit.target`, so every unit that uses a wired path starts after it; it runs only where the config volume is (`ConditionPathExists=`), and its failure exits the container non-zero (`FailureAction=exit-force`) rather than letting services write into the image layer. It runs on every boot: a container's mounts and account do not survive a restart or a rebuild. Everything it wires comes from the **bootstrap**, `sandbox.json`, which carries the whole create-time config: the config is complete before the wiring runs because the bootstrap carries it, not because the flow fetches it first ([ADR 26-10-08-127](../docs/adr/26-10-08-127-a-sandboxs-bootstrap-is-static-and-the-intake-carries-the-rest.md) §2). Nothing that can change while the sandbox exists is read here — secrets and the proxy credential arrive through the intake once the agent is up. Where there is nothing to wire — a VM guest boots its own init, and its backend places `sandbox.json` through the running guest ([ADR 26-10-09-143](../docs/adr/26-10-09-143-a-vm-sandbox-starts-its-agent-when-its-bootstrap-arrives.md) §1) — **`Provision`** does the same provisioning from the agent's own start: the user and its groups, the working root, the home skeleton, `~/.gitconfig`, direnv config and launchers, and the session-bus and desktop drop-ins — then, systemd having been up since boot, a `daemon-reload`, the session bus's socket recreated for the user, and the proxy-trust environment rendered, which its unit skipped at boot — and nothing wired (no declared volumes, ADR 0126 §2; sources arrive through the intake). It runs once per sandbox: the box's provisioning records (`provision.Records`, `/opt/discobox/provision/sandbox`, on the root filesystem) name the sandbox the disk was provisioned for, so an agent restart (the user's processes running) or a stop and start does not redo it; a disk provisioned before the records were kept carries the `/var/lib/discobox/provisioned` marker they replaced into them once, and the marker is removed. A config volume says `Wire` ran, and then it does nothing; it provisions only a Linux guest, since a macOS or Windows sandbox has one account, the image's (ADR 0145 §5). Also the **export mode**, `discobox-sandbox-agent export <subtree>...` (`export.go`, [ADR 0129](../docs/adr/0129-the-sandbox-agent-reads-the-tree-an-export-carries.md)): PID 1 of a one-shot container the pool agent starts from the sandbox base image, with the agent of the sandbox's platform pin bound in, to read a stopped sandbox's tree. It resolves the declared volumes exactly as `Wire` does — only the sandbox can say where a `%HOME%` path lives — with the user from the `DISCOBOX_USER_*` environment the pool agent gives it, then writes `data` and/or `sources` from the primary volumes to stdout as a `sandboxtree` archive, leaving out each `excludeFromExport` data path's `volumeDir`. It wires, chowns and starts nothing; the trees are mounted read-only, and only the archive goes to stdout, so everything it says goes to stderr, which the pool agent reports when it fails. **`ClearCaches`** is a machine pool's clear-cache, which the server's `POST .../cache/clear` runs: it empties every cache path the bootstrap declares, in place — the declared path, never the volume behind it, so it is the same on a box that wired its volumes and one that did not — keeping each directory, and touches no data path ([ADR 26-10-23-551](../docs/adr/26-10-23-551-a-vm-pool-bootstraps-its-own-agent-from-a-bundle-and-provisions-its-machines.md) §3: a machine's caches are on its own disk). |
sandbox-agent/DESIGN.md:36:| `sourceconverge` | Materializing as convergence ([ADR 0126](../docs/adr/0126-a-sandbox-does-not-share-a-host-or-a-filesystem-with-its-pool.md) §4): for each source the applied runtime-config document names with an origin, clone it onto its `target`, check out the pin (on `sandbox.json`'s `refName` when it is a branch, detached otherwise), restore its dirty-workspace snapshot, set up its remotes — `origin` as the source's own remote beside the pool remote the manifest names (`poolRemote`, ADR 26-10-10-545 §6), or for a source delivered before that the pool as `origin` and the remote as `upstream` — and write `sandboxconfig.SourceMaterializedMarker` inside its `.git`, holding the commit materialized — once. Every later pass only asserts the remote the checkout reaches its pool under (URL, default refspec, credential helper), because re-materializing would discard the sandbox's work; a `.git` carrying neither that marker nor this package's in-progress one is someone else's: one with a commit checked out and an `origin` that is a filesystem path is a checkout a pool made before it marked what it materialized, adopted as it stands — marked at what it has checked out, its `origin` asserted — and any other is refused, not reset. A materialized checkout with no HEAD for its pool remote — cloned before the pool pointed the origin's HEAD at what arrived — gets one (`remote set-head --auto`) on a later pass. git runs as the **owner of the target** (the sandbox user, resolved with its home and groups, when that is who it is), with the sandbox's own env so the clone takes the proxy route a user's git does — no chown afterwards, no `safe.directory`. The origin is asked for its refs first (`ls-remote`): one with none yet (a push not landed) is `waiting` and changes nothing. A clone then lands in a scratch directory of its own *inside* the target (the target can be a mount point, which a rename does not cross) — `.discobox-materializing-*`, uniquely named per attempt and carrying a marker file, so only directories the agent made are ever removed — with no checkout, and its `.git` is renamed into place only once whole, so an interrupted clone never leaves a partial `.git` that fails every retry (#30). Everything after the rename writes the tracked tree whole — `checkout --force` at the pin, `restore --worktree` from the snapshot — and never cleans, so files the target held before the clone survive the first attempt and every retry, and a retry simply goes on from the checkout. The materialized marker is written under the converger's lock and only when the current document still names the same target, origin and pin: a document that re-pins a source while an attempt runs leaves that attempt unfinished, and the next pass goes on from its checkout to the new pin. A pass runs on every delivered document and again, backing off to two minutes, while any source is `failed` or `waiting` on an origin; per-source state (`waiting`/`cloning`/`materialized`/`failed`, the commit the marker records, the error, the revision, and while cloning how far the clone has got) rides the status poll as `sourceStates`. The clone runs with `--progress` in git's own words (`LC_ALL=C`), and its stderr is parsed as it arrives: each meter (`counting` for the remote's enumerate/count/compress, `receiving`, `resolving`) updates the cloning state's progress, and only git's other lines are kept for the error, so the pool can say how far a minutes-long clone of a remote has got. The pool reads the same states on demand through `GET .../sources` (`runtime-config` scope), which it waits on while it settles a create. A materialized source is **not** the ready signal: the pool reads its project layer through `GET .../sources/{slug}/project-layer` — the source's `.discobox/settings.json`, or the `project.json` it replaces when there is none, found by `sandboxconfig.ReadSettings` and decoded by its `Settings`, answering the project layer alone and none when it sets nothing (a repository holding both kinds is a 422, and the old file alone is logged as a warning) — (`runtime-config` scope, checked before any other path test because a slug can spell one; read through an `os.Root` so a symlink cannot reach outside the checkout; 409 until materialized), settles the spec, and only then sets `Delivered` (ADR 0055). **Origin credentials** never enter the checkout: each origin that takes a token (`originToken`) is configured with `credential.<originUrl>.helper` set to an empty value (clearing any helper configured before it, so a user's `store` is never handed the token) and then this binary's `git-credential` mode, plus `useHttpPath`; the helper asks the agent over `/run/discobox/git-credential/credential.sock` for the token of the origin git names and answers it as a bearer credential (`authtype=Bearer`, `ephemeral`), so it needs git 2.46 or later. An origin without one — a remote-URL source — gets no helper configuration at all, so the user's own helper for it stands. The socket answers any account in the sandbox: a token fetches only this sandbox's own origins, which anyone there can already do. |

Update a pool.

--egress-allow, --egress-deny-by-default and --egress-passthrough set the pool's
egress level, which every discobox in the pool converges onto, running ones
included. A build's own base-image pulls are not filtered by any level (ADR
26-10-01-032 §7).

Egress is decided per discobox from four levels: its project, its pool, its
harness, and its own. A discobox is restricted when any level sets
--egress-deny-by-default, and then reaches only the union of every level's
--egress-allow entries and the hosts its harness image declares; an allow list
alone restricts nothing. An entry is a host ("github.com" is that host alone),
a wildcard ("*.github.com", "registry.*", "*"), an IP, or a CIDR, never a port.
--egress-allow replaces this level's list; on an update, --clear-egress-allow
empties it.

--egress-passthrough names hosts whose HTTPS proxy CONNECT is spliced to the
origin unread instead of intercepted, so TLS stays end to end (ADR
26-10-31-819): for a client that pins its certificate, or a protocol the proxy
does not read. It never admits a host, and nothing inside such a tunnel is read:
no credential is swapped into it, and only the connection, its TLS hello, and
its byte counts are audited. A discobox a person creates passes through every
level's hosts; one a discobox created, only its own level's, which a discobox
may set only to hosts its own passthrough covers. On an update,
--clear-egress-passthrough empties this level's list.

content.text:
Your dev server restarted during the pool rebuild, and that's likely my doing. I haven't found why the pool hasn't recovered since.

**Timeline:**
- **06:34:45 UTC (23:34 local):** after you deleted the machines, the server recreated the pool machine `dvm-prov-te6754gkjpyzjxfx--pool-dfqcve6ztdsmgbd6`. It copied over the pool's key and config and checked the machine's platform twice (the `uname -m; hostname` lines in your paste, the last at 06:34:59).
- **23:37–23:38 local:** your `task dev` loop rebuilt and restarted `discobox-server` (the running one started at 23:38:02). That was almost certainly triggered by my edits to `sandbox-agent`. The restart landed while the server was still setting up the new pool machine.
- **Since then:** the machine has sat untouched. It has no `/opt/discobox` and no pool agent, so it never reports, and the pool stays `offline`. The server has made no further calls to the machine in over 10 minutes. The pool record shows no error either, just "pool agent has not reported since 06:33:45".

The 502s you saw were boxd answering for the pool machine's address while nothing on it was serving yet.

The server's log only goes to your `task dev` terminal, so I can't see why it never picks the pool up again. Could you paste any server lines mentioning `pool_dfqcve6ztdsmgbd6` from 23:38 on? That would show whether it retries and fails, or never tries at all. If it never tries, that's a separate bug: a reconcile interrupted mid-setup isn't resumed after a restart. I'd look at that next.

To unstick it now, the repair path should rebuild the pool machine. If nothing kicks it, deleting just the pool machine again (`dvm-prov-…--pool-dfqcve6ztdsmgbd6`) with the dev loop idle should make the server recreate it from scratch. I'm not editing anything else right now, so another rebuild won't interrupt it.

**The two fixes you asked for are done, uncommitted:**
1. **Missing source directory:** this is what broke both your skills source and `discobox-ai/discobox` as the primary. The cloner (`sandbox-agent/sourceconverge/converge.go`) now creates a source's directory, and any missing parents, owned by the sandbox user, when nothing has created it. On a VM box nothing ever does.
2. **Desktop and session-bus ownership:** these settings (`sandbox-agent/boot/desktop.go`, `sessionbus.go`) are now written whether or not the desktop is installed yet. On a VM box the desktop installs later in the background, and systemd applies the settings once its services appear. The session-bus restart only runs when that service is already installed.

I added a test for a missing directory and updated one old test that relied on it being missing. I also updated `sandbox-agent/DESIGN.md`. Under `nix develop`, the `boot`, `sourceconverge` and `desktop` package tests pass; I didn't rerun the other modules myself. `check-hooks` still lists the full-suite hook as failed, with empty output. The run I could read before that showed only failures from running outside the Nix shell, but I haven't confirmed this one: `go tool task rerun-hooks` inside `nix develop` should settle it. None of this has been tried on a real boxd box yet, because the pool is down.

I'll find why the server never goes back to finish the pool machine.

content.text:
The `boxd` pool is working again (`HEALTH ready`, `READY true`). Try launching a box now. It's the first real test of the two box-side fixes, so I haven't seen a box start on boxd yet.

**What I did:** I deleted the empty pool machine again. The server then built a fresh one (`79efc609…`) with a new key, and the pool agent reported in at 23:54.

**Why it never recovered:** the server keeps a record, on the pool's database row, of what it installed on the pool machine.
1. After you deleted the machines, the server built a new pool machine. It was cut off before saving its record when `task dev` restarted the server (probably because of my edits).
2. After the restart, the server found a machine under the same name and copied its ID into the old record, keeping the old "pool agent is installed" entry. From then on every pass thought the machine was fully set up and did nothing.

**Fix (`server/providers/discovm/poolmachine.go`):** if the record names a different machine than the one actually there, the server now sets it up from scratch, as if it had just created it. That includes a new key and revoking the old one. A new test, `TestFakePoolMachineReplacedUnderItsRecordIsPlacedAgain`, passes, but I didn't check that it fails without the fix. Your pool's record had already been rewritten with the new ID, so this fix couldn't rescue it; deleting the machine did.

**All changes so far, uncommitted:**
1. The sandbox agent no longer crashes when the desktop isn't installed yet (`sandbox-agent/boot/boot.go`).
2. Desktop and session-bus services are set to run as your user even when the desktop installs after first boot (`sandbox-agent/boot/desktop.go`, `sessionbus.go`).
3. The agent creates a source's directory before cloning into it, which fixes both your skills source and `discobox-ai/discobox` as the main repo (`sandbox-agent/sourceconverge/converge.go`, plus a test).
4. The server notices a pool machine replaced under its record (above).
5. `sandbox-agent/DESIGN.md` is updated for 2 and 3.

The `discovm`, `boot`, `sourceconverge` and `desktop` package tests pass under `nix develop`. `check-hooks` still shows the full-suite hook as failed with empty output, and I haven't rerun it since. Separately, `station76` has several older `discobox-server` processes, one from Oct 24; they look like other checkouts' dev servers, and I left them alone.

sandbox-agent/DESIGN.md:36:| `sourceconverge` | Materializing as convergence ([ADR 0126](../docs/adr/0126-a-sandbox-does-not-share-a-host-or-a-filesystem-with-its-pool.md) §4): for each source the applied runtime-config document names with an origin, clone it onto its `target` — made, with any parent it lacks, and given to the sandbox user where nothing wired it, as in a VM guest, which has no sources volume — check out the pin (on `sandbox.json`'s `refName` when it is a branch, detached otherwise), restore its dirty-workspace snapshot, set up its remotes — `origin` as the source's own remote beside the pool remote the manifest names (`poolRemote`, ADR 26-10-10-545 §6), or for a source delivered before that the pool as `origin` and the remote as `upstream` — and write `sandboxconfig.SourceMaterializedMarker` inside its `.git`, holding the commit materialized — once. Every later pass only asserts the remote the checkout reaches its pool under (URL, default refspec, credential helper), because re-materializing would discard the sandbox's work; a `.git` carrying neither that marker nor this package's in-progress one is someone else's: one with a commit checked out and an `origin` that is a filesystem path is a checkout a pool made before it marked what it materialized, adopted as it stands — marked at what it has checked out, its `origin` asserted — and any other is refused, not reset. A materialized checkout with no HEAD for its pool remote — cloned before the pool pointed the origin's HEAD at what arrived — gets one (`remote set-head --auto`) on a later pass. git runs as the **owner of the target** (the sandbox user, resolved with its home and groups, when that is who it is), with the sandbox's own env so the clone takes the proxy route a user's git does — no chown afterwards, no `safe.directory`. The origin is asked for its refs first (`ls-remote`): one with none yet (a push not landed) is `waiting` and changes nothing. A clone then lands in a scratch directory of its own *inside* the target (the target can be a mount point, which a rename does not cross) — `.discobox-materializing-*`, uniquely named per attempt and carrying a marker file, so only directories the agent made are ever removed — with no checkout, and its `.git` is renamed into place only once whole, so an interrupted clone never leaves a partial `.git` that fails every retry (#30). Everything after the rename writes the tracked tree whole — `checkout --force` at the pin, `restore --worktree` from the snapshot — and never cleans, so files the target held before the clone survive the first attempt and every retry, and a retry simply goes on from the checkout. The materialized marker is written under the converger's lock and only when the current document still names the same target, origin and pin: a document that re-pins a source while an attempt runs leaves that attempt unfinished, and the next pass goes on from its checkout to the new pin. A pass runs on every delivered document and again, backing off to two minutes, while any source is `failed` or `waiting` on an origin; per-source state (`waiting`/`cloning`/`materialized`/`failed`, the commit the marker records, the error, the revision, and while cloning how far the clone has got) rides the status poll as `sourceStates`. The clone runs with `--progress` in git's own words (`LC_ALL=C`), and its stderr is parsed as it arrives: each meter (`counting` for the remote's enumerate/count/compress, `receiving`, `resolving`) updates the cloning state's progress, and only git's other lines are kept for the error, so the pool can say how far a minutes-long clone of a remote has got. The pool reads the same states on demand through `GET .../sources` (`runtime-config` scope), which it waits on while it settles a create. A materialized source is **not** the ready signal: the pool reads its project layer through `GET .../sources/{slug}/project-layer` — the source's `.discobox/settings.json`, or the `project.json` it replaces when there is none, found by `sandboxconfig.ReadSettings` and decoded by its `Settings`, answering the project layer alone and none when it sets nothing (a repository holding both kinds is a 422, and the old file alone is logged as a warning) — (`runtime-config` scope, checked before any other path test because a slug can spell one; read through an `os.Root` so a symlink cannot reach outside the checkout; 409 until materialized), settles the spec, and only then sets `Delivered` (ADR 0055). **Origin credentials** never enter the checkout: each origin that takes a token (`originToken`) is configured with `credential.<originUrl>.helper` set to an empty value (clearing any helper configured before it, so a user's `store` is never handed the token) and then this binary's `git-credential` mode, plus `useHttpPath`; the helper asks the agent over `/run/discobox/git-credential/credential.sock` for the token of the origin git names and answers it as a bearer credential (`authtype=Bearer`, `ephemeral`), so it needs git 2.46 or later. An origin without one — a remote-URL source — gets no helper configuration at all, so the user's own helper for it stands. The socket answers any account in the sandbox: a token fetches only this sandbox's own origins, which anyone there can already do. |

(`GET .../sources`, pool-signed, `runtime-config` scope), reads the primary
  source's project layer from it (`GET .../sources/{slug}/project-layer`), and
  compares it with the digest of the layer the container was built from
  (`discobox.project_layer` label). The same layer marks every source delivered;
  a different one is recorded in `project-layer.json` and the container is
  rebuilt against a bootstrap carrying it, once per create. A source the
  sandbox fails to clone `sourceFailureLimit` times, or has not begun after
  `sourceWaitingTimeout`, fails the create with what the sandbox said; the
  agent keeps retrying regardless. An agent that cannot report its sources at
  all (404 or 503: an image from before the route) fails the create at once
  with `ErrSourceStatesUnsupported`.
- **A pushed source parks.** Until the client's push lands in its bare origin
  there is nothing to clone and nothing settles. A source that names its
  branch has its origin's HEAD there from `initGitOrigin` on; one that names
  none has HEAD pointed at what arrived (`headOriginAtWhatArrived`, git in the
  pool's own repository) by whichever settles it first. The sandbox's agent may
  clone the moment the push lands; the resume create delivers the document
  again — a delivery wakes an agent backing off — and settles as above, and the
  agent fills in an `origin/HEAD` its early clone could not resolve.
- **Settling a start** (`settleConverged`): a sandbox started rather than
  created — unarchived or imported, whose create did not start it — has nobody
  waiting on it, so the status poll's convergence settles it once the sandbox
  reports every source materialized. With no create request in hand a
  container pool cannot rebuild, so a layer that needs one removes the
  container (`removeForRebuild`) for the control plane to recreate from the
  recorded layer; a machine pool makes the machine again in place itself, from
  the bootstrap it kept (`rebuildForProjectLayer`). It takes the primary's slug from `project-layer.json`, and settles
  nothing for a record from before that named one: only a create can say.
- **Upgrade.** A checkout a pool cloned before this keeps the empty marker it
  wrote, which the agent reads as materialized; one from before the marker —
  a commit checked out and an `origin` that is a filesystem path — is adopted

4. **A deleted pool machine wasn't rebuilt properly** if the server restarted mid-build (`server/providers/discovm/poolmachine.go`).
5. **Every fresh boxd box failed its create.** Ubuntu's git can't send the pool's token, and the newer git takes about 2.5 minutes to install in the background, so the pool gave up after three fast failures. While git is too old, the box now reports its sources as waiting, with the reason, and the pool keeps waiting (`sourceconverge/converge.go`, `git.go`, `pool-agent/sandboxruntime/sources.go`).

7. **The repos came back empty.** Only the Docker runtime recorded which repos a box gets from the pool's git cache, so on a VM box the pool served an empty repository. That step now runs for both runtimes (`pool-agent/sandboxruntime/runtime.go`, `origin.go`, `machine.go`).

content.text:
You're right that machines were being orphaned, but not from a gap at creation time, and the fix is made.

**Creation was fine.** Each box's machine is named from its box ID (`dvm-pool-<pool>--sbx-<id>`), and the box ID exists on the server before the machine is created. So the server can always find a box's machine, failed creates included.

**Note that `discobox rm` archives a box rather than deleting it.** On a VM pool, archiving deliberately keeps the machine, stopped, so the box can be brought back on the same disk. The server deletes archived boxes after 24 hours by default, and that deletion removes the machine. So the three stopped machines are expected, and all six go when their archives expire.

**The bug is the three still running** (`frnx1w52`, `78p9jwvw`, `gt6pb3b4`):
- On the pool machine, archive first checked for the box's state directory and answered "not found" without it. It never looked for the machine itself, unlike delete, which finds machines by name.
- The server treats "not found" from archive as "nothing to tear down" and marks the box archived.
- Those three were created by the pool machine I deleted and rebuilt yesterday, so their state directories were gone. Archiving them did nothing, reported success, and left them running.

**Fix (`pool-agent/sandboxruntime/machine.go`, `ArchiveSandbox`):** when the directory is missing, archive now looks up the machine by name. If it exists, archive recreates the directory, marks the box archived, and stops the machine. "Not found" now means only that there's neither a directory nor a machine, so the server's handling becomes correct. A new test covers both cases, the pool-agent runtime tests pass, and `pool-agent/DESIGN.md` is updated. I haven't tried it on boxd, and nothing is committed.

The fix won't reach those three: their boxes are already marked archived, so nothing archives them again. They'll keep running until their archives expire within 24 hours, which deletes them. Want me to stop them now with `boxd machine stop`? That's reversible.

One related gap: a box's state on a VM pool lives only on the pool machine's disk, so replacing the pool machine loses it. Archive and delete now cope by finding machines by name. But unarchiving one of those boxes, or the status checks that read that state, would act on an empty record. Keeping that record on the server or in the box's own machine would close it properly; that's a design change I haven't made.
but archived boxes are not deleted, right? they should be stopped.

Right, archiving doesn't delete a box: on a VM pool it stops the machine and keeps it, so the box can be brought back on the same disk. That's how it works in the code and what the fix enforces.

The one thing I said that may have sounded different: an archive isn't kept forever. After the project's archive retention runs out (24 hours by default, `DefaultArchiveRetention` in `server/internal/resources/sandboxes/archive.go`), the server deletes the box, and that's when its machine is removed. Until then it should sit stopped.

So for what's on boxd now:
- **`sbx-m9x8q65r`, `sbx-82xxbeex`, `sbx-d0jamqtg`:** stopped, which is correct.
- **`sbx-frnx1w52`, `sbx-78p9jwvw`, `sbx-gt6pb3b4`:** running, which is the bug I fixed. With the fix, archiving one of these stops its machine even when the pool has lost its record of the box.

The fix applies on the next archive, and these three are already marked archived, so it won't stop them. Want me to stop those three machines now?
